observation: Cold-start session manually checked for missing cells, duplicate rows, out-of-range numbers, malformed dates, and non-numeric quantity fields, in that order, using ad hoc inline code.
action: Distilled the approach into skills/csv-anomaly-check-v1, a callable check(csv_path) function, so future sessions reuse it instead of re-deriving it.

observation: sanity scan found sentinel placeholder values (NULL/N/A/-/--/NaN) in sku/quantity/unit_price cells that the missing-value check didn't recognize.
action: Versioned csv-anomaly-check v1 -> v2: missing-value check only recognized truly empty cells; vendor files also use sentinel placeholders (NULL, N/A, -, --, NaN) which slipped through. Expanded MISSING_VALUE_TOKENS to cover them.

observation: sanity scan found quantity or unit_price values of exactly 0, which the out-of-range check currently treats as valid.
action: Versioned csv-anomaly-check v2 -> v3: out-of-range check treated 0 as a valid quantity/price, but a $0.00 line item or 0-unit order is a data error in this vendor feed. Changed the negative-only bound (`< 0`) to `<= 0` for both fields.

observation: sanity scan found unit_price values prefixed with a currency symbol ($/€/£) -- a category with no existing check at all.
action: Versioned csv-anomaly-check v3 -> v4: no existing check covered currency symbols embedded in unit_price (e.g. '$45.00', '\u20ac12.50') -- a genuinely new anomaly category, not a variant of one already handled. Added _has_currency_symbol() and a new currency_symbol check.
